clinical_notes: 38 y/o with reflux symptoms responsive to PPI for 8 weeks. Provider requesting EGD with biopsy to evaluate for esophagitis. Patient is otherwise healthy, no alarm features (no dysphagia, no weight loss, no GI bleeding, no anemia). Family history negative for upper GI cancer. Patient requests the procedure for reassurance.
ground_truth_reasoning: Indication 1 NOT met: patient is 38, below age >=50 threshold.
Indication 2 NOT met: no alarm features, no family history.
Routine EGD <50 without alarms is excluded → DENIED.
policy_excerpt:
Aetna Commercial Coverage 0103 — Upper GI Endoscopy.
Indication 1: Persistent reflux symptoms despite >=8 weeks PPI therapy AND age >=50, OR
Indication 2: Any age with documented alarm features (dysphagia, odynophagia, unintentional weight loss >5% body weight, hematemesis, melena, iron-deficiency anemia, or first-degree family history of esophageal/gastric cancer).
Routine screening EGD without alarm features in patients <50 is not covered regardless of symptom duration.

clinical_notes: 62 y/o with bilateral knee osteoarthritis, right worse than left. Failed acetaminophen and PT for 8 weeks. Provider requesting intra-articular hyaluronic acid injection. Patient had a prior hyaluronic acid injection series in the same knee 4 months ago with documented partial relief. Provider notes the prior injection 'helped some' and is requesting a second series.
ground_truth_reasoning: Repeat series eligibility: 6-month interval — only 4 months have passed since prior series.
Even if interval were met, response criterion requires quantified >=50% pain reduction or >=20pt WOMAC improvement.
Notes document only subjective 'helped some' — does not satisfy the quantitative criterion.
Both criteria fail → DENIED.
policy_excerpt:
UnitedHealthcare Commercial Medical Policy: Intra-Articular Hyaluronic Acid Injections.
Coverage: Repeat injection series may be authorized once per 6-month interval per knee, contingent on documented >=50% pain reduction or >=20-point WOMAC improvement from the prior series. Subjective reports of 'partial relief' or 'helped some' without quantified functional improvement do not satisfy the response criterion.

clinical_notes: 44 y/o male with right knee medial meniscal tear confirmed on MRI 6 weeks ago. Pain and mechanical symptoms (catching). Completed 4 weeks of PT without improvement. Provider requesting arthroscopic partial meniscectomy. Patient also has BMI 38, A1C 9.2%, smokes 1 PPD.
ground_truth_reasoning: Indication criteria (1) and (2) met: mechanical symptoms, MRI-confirmed meniscal tear.
Perioperative prerequisite (a) FAILED: A1C 9.2% > 8.0.
Smoking cessation counseling not documented either.
Any failed prerequisite → DENIED. Patient may resubmit after glycemic optimization.
policy_excerpt:
BCBS Surgical Policy: Knee Arthroscopy.
Coverage requires:
(1) Documented mechanical symptoms or persistent pain >=6 weeks despite conservative care.
(2) MRI confirmation of meniscal pathology.
PERIOPERATIVE PREREQUISITES (all required):
(a) HbA1c <8.0 within 30 days of surgery for diabetic patients;
(b) BMI <40 for elective ASC procedures;
(c) Smoking cessation counseling documented within 60 days.
Failure of any perioperative prerequisite results in denial; patient may resubmit after meeting criteria.

clinical_notes: 51 y/o with right L5 radiculopathy confirmed by EMG. Failed 8 weeks PT, NSAIDs, and a Medrol dose pack. Provider requesting transforaminal epidural steroid injection at L5. Patient is on apixaban 5mg BID for atrial fibrillation. Provider notes he will hold apixaban for 24 hours pre-procedure.
ground_truth_reasoning: Indication criteria met: EMG-confirmed radiculopathy, failed conservative trial.
Anticoagulation contraindication: provider plans 24-hour hold but ASRA guidelines (cited in policy) require 3 days off apixaban for transforaminal injection.
Insufficient interruption is a hard contraindication → DENIED.
policy_excerpt:
Cigna Coverage Policy 0163: Spinal Injections.
Indications: Radicular pain refractory to >=6 weeks conservative therapy, with EMG or imaging correlate.
ANTICOAGULATION REQUIREMENT: Patients on direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs including apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, edoxaban) must hold the medication for the duration specified by the most recent ASRA Pain Medicine guidelines: apixaban requires 3 days off prior to neuraxial or transforaminal injection (NOT 24 hours). Insufficient anticoagulant interruption is a hard contraindication.

clinical_notes: 68 y/o with newly diagnosed prostate adenocarcinoma. Gleason 3+3=6, PSA 6.2, clinical stage T1c. Patient and oncologist have elected definitive radiation therapy. Provider requesting IMRT (intensity-modulated radiation therapy).
ground_truth_reasoning: Patient is low-risk: PSA 6.2 (<=10), Gleason 6 (<=6), T1c (<=T2a) — meets all three low-risk criteria.
Policy specifies 3D-CRT (77385) for low-risk disease, not IMRT (77386).
IMRT not medically necessary for this risk stratum → DENIED. Resubmission with CPT 77385 likely covered.
policy_excerpt:
Medicare NCD 220.5: External Beam Radiation Therapy for Prostate Cancer.
IMRT covered for prostate cancer when ANY of: (a) high-risk disease (PSA >20, Gleason >=8, or stage T2c+), (b) intermediate-risk with documented anatomic complexity precluding 3D-CRT delivery, (c) post-prostatectomy salvage setting.
For low-risk disease (PSA <=10 AND Gleason <=6 AND <=T2a) IMRT is not medically necessary; conventional 3D conformal therapy (3D-CRT, CPT 77385) is the appropriate technique.

clinical_notes: 47 y/o with right shoulder pain x 6 months. Provider requesting 12 PT visits over 6 weeks. Patient has previously completed 30 PT visits over the prior 6 months for the same shoulder pain without improvement. Notes do not document a re-evaluation or change in treatment plan from the prior course.
ground_truth_reasoning: Patient has already received 30 PT visits for this condition.
Policy requires independent specialist re-evaluation after 30 visits before additional PT.
Notes do not document the re-evaluation or any objective functional improvement from prior course.
Continued PT criteria unmet → DENIED for missing info.
policy_excerpt:
Aetna Outpatient Rehabilitation Policy.
Initial PT: up to 12 visits per body region per episode.
Continued PT: requires re-evaluation documenting (a) measurable objective improvement in functional status from baseline, (b) updated treatment plan reflecting current deficits, and (c) reasonable expectation of further improvement. PT for maintenance of chronic stable conditions is not covered. Patients who have not improved after 30 visits for a single condition require independent specialist re-evaluation before additional PT will be authorized.

clinical_notes: 62 y/o with 4 weeks of low back pain that became progressively worse. Started PT 3 weeks ago, completed 6 sessions. Now reporting new right foot drop over the past week, with documented 3/5 tibialis anterior weakness on exam, 4/5 extensor hallucis longus weakness, and dermatomal L5 sensory loss. Provider requesting urgent lumbar MRI.
ground_truth_reasoning: Conservative therapy <6 weeks (only 3 weeks PT) — would normally fail C.1.
C.2 NEUROLOGICAL OVERRIDE applies: documented progressive motor deficit AND acute foot drop — TWO independent override criteria.
C.2 explicitly waives the conservative therapy requirement.
→ APPROVED under the override clause.
policy_excerpt:
CMS LCD L34522 §C.1: Conservative therapy >=6 weeks required before lumbar MRI for nonspecific low back pain.
§C.2 (NEUROLOGICAL OVERRIDE): The conservative therapy requirement is WAIVED when the clinical presentation includes any of the following: (a) progressive motor deficit documented over consecutive visits, (b) cauda equina symptoms, (c) suspected epidural abscess or hematoma, (d) acute foot drop, (e) post-traumatic radiculopathy. These indications represent surgical emergencies or evolving deficits where delayed imaging risks permanent injury.

clinical_notes: 34 y/o with new headache x 2 days. No prior headache history. Reports the worst headache of her life, sudden onset while exercising. No fever, no rash. Exam: photophobia, mild neck stiffness, no focal deficit. CT head without contrast read as normal at the outside ED 24 hours ago. Provider requesting brain MRI with and without contrast to evaluate for vascular abnormality.
ground_truth_reasoning: Surface read: routine imaging for headache is excluded.
BUT: thunderclap onset (exception (a)) AND meningismus on exam (exception (g)) — TWO independent exception criteria met.
Negative CT >6 hours after onset does not rule out vascular etiology — MRI/MRA explicitly indicated by policy.
→ APPROVED.

clinical_notes: 58 y/o male presented to ED with crushing substernal chest pain at rest, troponin elevated to 1.8 (normal <0.04), ECG with new T-wave inversions in V3-V6. Hemodynamically stable. Cardiology consulted, recommends urgent left heart catheterization. No prior stress testing has been performed.
ground_truth_reasoning: Surface read: no prior stress test → fail elective criterion.
BUT: NSTEMI (troponin 1.8, new T-wave changes) = ACS with biomarker elevation → exception (a) applies.
Stress-test prerequisite is for ELECTIVE evaluation only; urgent ACS bypass is explicitly covered.
→ APPROVED.
policy_excerpt:
UnitedHealthcare Cardiac Catheterization Policy.
ELECTIVE catheterization requires prior non-invasive risk stratification (stress test, CCTA, or myocardial perfusion imaging) demonstrating ischemia or high-risk anatomy.
URGENT/EMERGENT catheterization without prior stress testing is COVERED for any of: (a) acute coronary syndrome with biomarker elevation, (b) acute ST-elevation MI, (c) hemodynamic instability suggesting cardiogenic shock, (d) post-arrest with shockable rhythm, (e) refractory chest pain despite maximal medical therapy. The requirement for prior stress testing applies only to elective evaluation of stable chest pain.

clinical_notes: 42 y/o with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis, EDSS 2.5. Failed glatiramer acetate (Copaxone) due to injection site reactions and subsequent breakthrough relapse on therapy. Provider requesting natalizumab (Tysabri) infusions. Patient is JCV antibody negative (recent test, index 0.2). MRI shows no new lesions. Provider notes the patient prefers monthly infusion to daily injection.
ground_truth_reasoning: (1) RRMS confirmed.
(2) JCV antibody negative (index 0.2 is negative).
(3) Failed glatiramer acetate (first-line) with BOTH intolerance (injection reactions) AND breakthrough relapse.
(4) Provider attestation expected at administration.
All criteria met → APPROVED. Patient preference is irrelevant to coverage but doesn't disqualify.

clinical_notes: 31 y/o female with systemic lupus erythematosus, severe lupus nephritis biopsy class IV. Failed mycophenolate mofetil with progression to nephrotic-range proteinuria. Rheumatology and nephrology jointly recommend belimumab as add-on therapy. Patient has not yet tried cyclophosphamide. State Medicaid step therapy normally requires cyclophosphamide trial before belimumab.
ground_truth_reasoning: Patient has not tried cyclophosphamide — would normally fail step therapy.
Override (d) applies: joint rheum + nephro recommendation is documented.
Override (a) potentially applies if there's any prior reaction but not documented in notes.
Override (d) alone is sufficient.
→ APPROVED.

clinical_notes: 67 y/o newly diagnosed non-small cell lung cancer, stage IIIA by CT and bronchoscopic biopsy. Provider requesting whole-body PET-CT for staging prior to definitive chemoradiation. Initial submission denied because policy requires staging PET only for stages I-II being considered for surgical resection. Provider appealed, citing the patient's stage IIIA classification and the role of PET in identifying occult metastases that would change the treatment intent from curative chemoradiation to palliative.
ground_truth_reasoning: Initial denial: Indication 1 only covers stages I-II, patient is IIIA.
Appeal cites Indication 2: Stage III NSCLC with treatment-intent decision (curative chemoradiation vs palliative).
Indication 2 is explicitly appeal-eligible.
Provider documents the curative-vs-palliative distinction.
→ OVERTURNED ON APPEAL.
policy_excerpt:
Aetna Imaging Coverage: PET-CT for Lung Cancer.
Coverage Indication 1: Initial staging in clinical stage I-II NSCLC being considered for surgical resection.
Coverage Indication 2 (APPEAL-ELIGIBLE): Stage III NSCLC when PET would alter the planned treatment intent (curative vs palliative). Initial denials under Indication 1 based on stage classification may be overturned on appeal when Indication 2 is invoked with documentation that the imaging would distinguish between locoregional disease appropriate for chemoradiation and metastatic disease appropriate for systemic therapy alone.
Coverage Indication 3: Treatment response assessment 12 weeks after definitive therapy.

clinical_notes: 76 y/o with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, previously treated with docetaxel and abiraterone. Now with rising PSA and new bone pain. Provider requesting lutetium-177 PSMA-617 (Pluvicto). Initial submission denied because policy requires PSMA-PET imaging confirmation, which the patient has not yet undergone. Provider appealed, noting the patient has a documented contrast allergy to gadolinium-based agents and is unable to tolerate the PET scanning protocol; additionally, the patient has prior bone scan and CT documenting PSMA-expressing metastatic disease pattern characteristic of PSMA+ tumor biology.
ground_truth_reasoning: Initial denial: no PSMA-PET confirmation.
Appeal: documented contrast allergy = PET contraindication.
Alternative imaging (bone scan, CT) shows metastatic pattern.
Both waiver conditions (contraindication AND alt imaging) met.
→ OVERTURNED ON APPEAL.
policy_excerpt:
Humana Specialty Drug Policy: Lu-177 PSMA-617 (Pluvicto).
Standard prerequisite: PSMA-PET confirmation of PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
PSMA-PET WAIVER (APPEAL-ELIGIBLE): The PSMA-PET requirement may be waived on appeal when the patient has a documented contraindication to PET imaging (severe contrast allergy, inability to lie still due to pain or claustrophobia refractory to sedation, dialysis-dependent renal failure) AND alternative imaging (bone scan, CT, MRI) demonstrates metastatic burden consistent with PSMA-expressing prostate adenocarcinoma.

clinical_notes: 71 y/o male with three-vessel coronary disease, EF 35%, diabetic, prior stroke. Cardiology evaluated for revascularization, concluded surgical CABG superior to PCI per SYNTAX score. Initial CABG authorization denied as 'PCI is the standard first-line approach.' Provider appealed citing the patient's diabetes, three-vessel disease, and reduced EF — all factors where guideline-directed therapy favors CABG over PCI.
ground_truth_reasoning: Initial denial: PCI-first generic preference.
Appeal: patient meets MULTIPLE Class I CABG indications: (a) three-vessel + diabetes, (c) EF 35% with multivessel.
Override criteria explicitly appeal-eligible.
→ OVERTURNED ON APPEAL.
policy_excerpt:
Medicare NCD: Coronary Revascularization Procedures.
Both PCI and CABG are covered for appropriate clinical indications. The choice between modalities follows ACC/AHA/SCAI guideline-directed appropriate use criteria.
APPEAL-ELIGIBLE OVERRIDE for CABG over PCI (Class I recommendations): (a) Three-vessel disease with diabetes, (b) Left main disease with SYNTAX score >32, (c) Reduced EF <=35% with multivessel disease, (d) Failed prior PCI of the same lesion, (e) Anatomy unsuitable for percutaneous approach.
Initial denials based on a generic PCI-first preference may be overturned when guideline-directed Class I CABG indications are documented.

clinical_notes: Pediatric patient (age 5) with suspected OSA. Provider orders unattended home sleep test (HSAT Type III). No prior in-lab PSG.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Polysomnography
Key complexity: Age restriction on HSAT
Trick clause: Agent must know HSAT is not validated/covered for children; in-lab PSG is required. Easy to miss age-based exclusion.
Correct determination: DENY (HSAT not validated for pediatrics)
policy_excerpt:
LCD L37044 — Home Sleep Apnea Testing (HSAT, CPT 95800/95806)

Coverage criteria:
1. Adult patients (age >=18) with high pre-test probability of moderate-to-severe OSA;
2. No significant comorbidities that would contraindicate ambulatory testing.

EXCLUSIONS — HSAT is NOT covered for any of:
- Pediatric patients (age <18). HSAT is not validated for children; facility-based in-lab PSG is required.
- Patients with significant cardiopulmonary disease (CHF NYHA III/IV, severe COPD, neuromuscular disease).
- Patients with suspected non-obstructive sleep disorders.

When an exclusion applies, in-lab PSG (CPT 95810) is the appropriate test.

clinical_notes: Patient has comorbid CHF (NYHA III) and suspected OSA. Provider orders HSAT instead of in-lab PSG.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Polysomnography
Key complexity: Comorbidity exclusion for HSAT
Trick clause: LCD excludes HSAT for patients with significant cardiopulmonary disease. Agent must flag CHF as disqualifying for home testing.
Correct determination: DENY (HSAT inappropriate for significant cardiopulmonary disease)

clinical_notes: Patient diagnosed with narcolepsy via clinical history only. Provider requests MSLT without preceding overnight PSG.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Polysomnography
Key complexity: MSLT prerequisite
Trick clause: MSLT is only covered when preceded by overnight PSG to rule out other sleep disorders. Agent may approve MSLT in isolation.
Correct determination: DENY (MSLT requires preceding nocturnal PSG)

clinical_notes: Patient with central sleep apnea (not obstructive) requests oral appliance E0486. AHI 22, all central events.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Oral Appliances (OSA)
Key complexity: Diagnosis mismatch
Trick clause: LCD specifically covers obstructive sleep apnea. Central apnea is a different pathophysiology not addressed by mandibular advancement.
Correct determination: DENY (oral appliances only covered for OSA)
policy_excerpt:
LCD L33611 — Oral Appliances: Covered Diagnoses

Oral mandibular advancement appliances (E0486) are covered exclusively for OBSTRUCTIVE sleep apnea (ICD-10 G47.33).

NOT COVERED for any of:
- Central sleep apnea (G47.31). Mandibular advancement addresses upper airway obstruction; central apnea is a different pathophysiology and oral appliances are not indicated.
- Mixed sleep apnea where central events predominate.
- Snoring without documented OSA.
- Insomnia or other non-respiratory sleep disorders.

clinical_notes: Oral appliance billed with E0485 (prefabricated) but documentation describes custom impressions, bite registration, and lab fabrication.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Oral Appliances (OSA)
Key complexity: Code vs documentation mismatch
Trick clause: Agent must detect CPT/HCPCS code mismatch with clinical documentation. Upcoding or downcoding issue.
Correct determination: FLAG/DENY (should be E0486 custom, not E0485 prefab)
policy_excerpt:
HCPCS Coding for Oral Appliances:

E0485 (Oral Device, Prefabricated): Covered for off-the-shelf, mass-produced devices that do not require dental impressions or laboratory fabrication.

E0486 (Oral Device, Custom Fabricated): Required when the device is constructed via dental impressions, bite registration, and laboratory fabrication. Custom devices documented as such must be billed under E0486, not E0485.

Code-documentation mismatch (billing E0485 when documentation describes custom impressions, bite registration, and lab fabrication) constitutes a coding error. The claim should be denied or recoded to E0486.

clinical_notes: Patient prescribed BiPAP (E0470) for OSA with AHI 18. No documented CPAP failure. Provider states patient 'prefers BiPAP.'
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: CPAP/BiPAP
Key complexity: Step therapy requirement
Trick clause: BiPAP for OSA requires prior CPAP trial failure. Patient preference alone doesn't meet medical necessity. Agent may miss step-therapy requirement.
Correct determination: DENY (BiPAP requires documented CPAP failure for OSA)

clinical_notes: Provider applies two different skin substitute products to the same wound on the same date of service. Bills for both.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Wound Care / Skin Substitutes
Key complexity: Stacking prohibition
Trick clause: LCDs prohibit applying multiple skin substitutes to same wound on same date. Agent must detect duplicate/stacked billing.
Correct determination: DENY one of the two (cannot stack skin substitutes on same wound same DOS)
policy_excerpt:
LCD L36690 — Skin Substitute Grafts

Skin substitute application is covered when documentation supports the indication and product selection. ONLY ONE skin substitute product may be applied to a single wound on a single date of service. Stacking multiple skin substitutes on the same wound on the same DOS is prohibited regardless of total wound area or product type.

When two products are billed for the same wound on the same date, one of the two must be denied. Provider should select the more appropriate product based on wound characteristics; the secondary product is non-covered. Sequential applications on different dates are acceptable when prior application has been evaluated and shown incomplete coverage or ongoing healing need.

clinical_notes: PET scan requested for initial staging of a newly diagnosed small (T1a) renal cell carcinoma. No metastatic symptoms.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Advanced Imaging
Key complexity: PET indication specificity
Trick clause: PET is not covered for initial staging of renal cell carcinoma per NCD. Agent must know cancer-specific PET indications rather than applying a blanket 'cancer = PET approved' rule.
Correct determination: DENY (PET not indicated for initial staging of small RCC)

clinical_notes: Cardiac MRI requested for a patient with chronic stable chest pain, normal stress test, normal echo, and normal coronary CTA performed 3 months ago.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Advanced Imaging
Key complexity: Redundant imaging
Trick clause: Multiple prior negative studies make cardiac MRI medically unnecessary. Agent must evaluate cumulative prior workup, not just the single request.
Correct determination: DENY (no incremental diagnostic value after comprehensive negative workup)

clinical_notes: Patient with BMI 33 and type 2 diabetes requests Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Documents show 4 months of supervised weight management (LCD requires 6 months).
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Bariatric Surgery
Key complexity: Duration of conservative therapy
Trick clause: BMI 33 with comorbidity can qualify, but 6 months of documented supervised nutrition is mandatory. 4 months is insufficient. Agent may round up or miss the duration check.
Correct determination: DENY (does not meet 6-month supervised diet requirement)

clinical_notes: Ozempic (semaglutide) prescribed for weight loss in a patient with BMI 28, no diabetes, no cardiovascular disease. Provider codes it as diabetes management but A1c is 5.2%.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Specialty Pharmacy
Key complexity: Diagnosis integrity / off-label
Trick clause: Agent must cross-reference the billed diagnosis against clinical data. A1c 5.2% contradicts diabetes diagnosis. This tests fraud detection capability.
Correct determination: DENY (fraudulent diagnosis coding; BMI <30 without comorbidity doesn't qualify for weight indication either)
policy_excerpt:
Specialty Drug Coverage: Semaglutide (Ozempic / Wegovy)

OZEMPIC (semaglutide for type 2 diabetes management):
Coverage requires documented type 2 diabetes mellitus (HbA1c >=6.5% on prior testing OR established diagnosis with current pharmacotherapy). Patients with HbA1c <6.5% and no prior diabetes diagnosis do not meet the diabetes indication.

WEGOVY (semaglutide for chronic weight management):
Coverage requires BMI >=30, OR BMI >=27 with at least one weight-related comorbidity (hypertension, dyslipidemia, cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes).

Diagnosis coding integrity: claims billing T2DM (E11.x) with current HbA1c <6.5% and no prior diabetes documentation may indicate diagnosis miscoding. Plans review such claims for fraud, waste, and abuse.

clinical_notes: Patient resides in Puerto Rico. Provider submits oral appliance claim to Noridian (J-D DME MAC). The applicable LCD is from CGS Administrators (J-C, which covers Puerto Rico for DME).
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Jurisdiction Conflict
Key complexity: Jurisdiction routing
Trick clause: Puerto Rico DME goes through CGS (J-C per L33611), not Noridian. Agent must validate correct jurisdictional assignment before applying LCD criteria.
Correct determination: FLAG — wrong MAC jurisdiction

clinical_notes: Prior auth submitted 3 days AFTER the oral appliance was delivered and fitted. Provider claims 'urgent medical necessity' but documentation shows routine scheduling.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Retroactive Auth
Key complexity: Retroactive PA policy
Trick clause: Most MACs deny retroactive PA for elective DME. Agent may incorrectly approve if it doesn't check service date vs auth request date.
Correct determination: DENY (retroactive PA not permitted for non-emergent DME)
policy_excerpt:
Prior Authorization Timing Requirements for DME

Prior authorization for durable medical equipment must be submitted and APPROVED before the date of service. Retroactive PA is generally NOT permitted for elective DME items.

Limited exceptions for retroactive consideration:
(a) Documented emergency / urgent medical necessity that precluded prior submission (must be supported by clinical documentation of the emergent presentation);
(b) Beneficiary eligibility was retroactively established after service;
(c) System or processing failure documented by the submitting provider.

Routine elective DME items delivered before the PA submission date are NOT eligible for retroactive PA. Convenience and provider scheduling do not constitute urgent medical necessity.

clinical_notes: Patient with OSA and chronic insomnia. Provider orders both PSG (covered under L33405) and cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia device (not covered under any LCD). Single combined claim submitted.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Overlapping LCDs
Key complexity: Unbundling / mixed coverage
Trick clause: Agent must parse a single claim with items falling under different coverage rules. Cannot blanket approve/deny the entire claim.
Correct determination: PARTIAL APPROVE — approve PSG, deny CBT-I device

clinical_notes: Patient has both OSA (AHI 12) and restless leg syndrome. Provider orders PSG + MSLT + actigraphy all on the same authorization. Actigraphy was removed from LCD coverage in R9 revision (07/01/2020).
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Overlapping LCDs
Key complexity: Retired coverage element
Trick clause: Agent must track LCD revision history — actigraphy was explicitly removed in the R9 revision. Also must evaluate MSLT indication independently.
Correct determination: APPROVE PSG, DENY MSLT (no narcolepsy indication), DENY actigraphy (removed from coverage)
policy_excerpt:
LCD L33405 — Sleep Studies (Revision History R9, eff. 07/01/2020)

Covered services:
1. Polysomnography (95810) — covered for OSA evaluation;
2. Multiple Sleep Latency Test (95805) — covered ONLY when the indication is suspected narcolepsy or idiopathic hypersomnia AND preceded by overnight PSG;
3. Maintenance of Wakefulness Test (95805) — covered for occupational fitness-for-duty in safety-sensitive roles.

REMOVED FROM COVERAGE in R9 revision (effective 07/01/2020):
- Actigraphy (95803) is no longer a covered diagnostic modality for sleep disorders. Prior to 07/01/2020 it was covered as an adjunct study; the R9 revision removed this coverage based on insufficient evidence of incremental diagnostic value.

Restless leg syndrome alone does not establish PSG or MSLT necessity.

clinical_notes: Oral appliance PA submitted with a valid sleep study showing AHI 15, physician order, and diagnosis of OSA — but the sleep study is dated 4 years ago. No recent clinical re-evaluation. Patient's weight has changed by +40 lbs since the study.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Documentation Gap
Key complexity: Stale diagnostic data
Trick clause: A 4-year-old sleep study with significant weight change may no longer reflect current disease severity. Agent must evaluate temporal validity of supporting documentation.
Correct determination: DENY or REQUEST UPDATED STUDY (clinical status has materially changed)
